title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction in General K-Algebras
description: Formalizes modular reduction via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras: evaluating f at x equals evaluating f mod minpoly(x). Also proves base change behavior in algebra towers K ⊂ L ⊂ A, showing degree can only decrease when extending the base field.

overview.historicalContext: The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element x in a K-algebra A generates the kernel of the evaluation map K[X] → A. Polynomial arithmetic modulo the minimal polynomial captures all algebraic relations satisfied by x. In a tower K ⊂ L ⊂ A, the minimal polynomial over L divides the base change of the one over K, so the degree can only decrease with larger base fields. The theory of minimal polynomials was central to Cayley and Hamilton's work on matrices in the 1850s-1860s; the Cayley-Hamilton theorem states that a matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial, and the minimal polynomial divides it. These results were generalized to abstract algebras by Noether and Artin in the 1920s-1930s, and the universal characterization via the kernel of the evaluation map is fundamental to modern commutative algebra.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize (1) modular reduction of polynomial evaluation via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras, and (2) base change behavior of minimal polynomials in algebra towers.
overview.text: Formalizes modular reduction via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras: evaluating f at x equals evaluating f mod minpoly(x). Also proves base change behavior in algebra towers K ⊂ L ⊂ A, showing degree can only decrease when extending the base field.
overview.proofStrategy: For modular reduction: use the division algorithm f = (f mod m) + m · q, then evaluate at x where m(x) = 0. For tower divisibility: map minpoly K x through algebraMap K L to get an annihilating polynomial over L, then apply the universal property of the minimal polynomial over L.
keyInsights: Evaluating f(x) only depends on f mod minpoly(x) — higher-degree information is annihilated
The annihilator ideal of x is exactly the principal ideal generated by the minimal polynomial
In algebra towers, the minimal polynomial degree can only decrease when extending the base field
Equality in towers holds precisely when the base-changed polynomial remains irreducible
The reduction theorem generalizes the Cayley-Hamilton corollary: any polynomial function of a matrix can be computed by a polynomial of degree less than the matrix size

sections.title: Documentation and Setup
sections.summary: Header documenting the five main results: reduction, annihilator characterization, congruence, power reduction, and degree bounds. Sets up universe-polymorphic variables for a field $K$ and $K$-algebra $A$
sections.mathContext: The setup `{K : Type*} [Field K] {A : Type*} [Ring A] [Algebra K A]` works in any $K$-algebra — not just matrix algebras, but field extensions, polynomial quotient rings, group algebras, etc.

sections.title: Section I: Core Reduction Theorem
sections.summary: The fundamental theorem: $\text{aeval}\ x\ f = \text{aeval}\ x\ (f \bmod \text{minpoly}\ K\ x)$. Uses the division algorithm $f = (f \bmod m) + m \cdot q$, then evaluates at $x$ where $m(x) = 0$
sections.mathContext: This says $f(x)$ depends only on $f \bmod \mu_x$ where $\mu_x = \text{minpoly}(K, x)$. Algebraically, the evaluation map $K[X] \to A$ factors through $K[X]/(\mu_x)$.

sections.title: Section II: Annihilator Characterization
sections.summary: Full characterization: $f(x) = 0 \iff \mu_x | f$. Shows the annihilator ideal $\text{Ann}(x) = (\mu_x)$ is principal. Closure under addition and multiplication follow
sections.mathContext: The annihilator ideal $\{f \in K[X] : f(x) = 0\}$ is exactly the principal ideal $(\mu_x)$, since $K[X]$ is a PID and $\mu_x$ is the monic generator of minimal degree.

sections.title: Section III: Congruence and Quotient Structure
sections.summary: $f(x) = g(x) \iff \mu_x | (f - g)$. This identifies the evaluation equivalence relation with congruence modulo $\mu_x$, making $K[X]/(\mu_x) \cong K[x] \subseteq A$ explicit
sections.mathContext: The congruence relation $f \equiv g \pmod{\mu_x}$ captures algebraic equality at $x$: the quotient ring $K[X]/(\mu_x)$ is isomorphic to the $K$-subalgebra generated by $x$.

sections.title: Section IV: Degree Bounds
sections.summary: The remainder $f \bmod \mu_x$ has degree $< \deg(\mu_x)$. In a domain, $\deg(\mu_x) > 0$ since $\mu_x$ is monic and irreducible (not a unit)
sections.mathContext: Every element of $K[x] \cong K[X]/(\mu_x)$ has a unique representative of degree $< \deg(\mu_x)$, forming a $K$-vector space of dimension $\deg(\mu_x)$.

sections.title: Section V: Power Reduction
sections.summary: Powers $x^k$ reduce via $x^k = (X^k \bmod \mu_x)(x)$, and $x$ itself reduces to $(X \bmod \mu_x)(x)$. This is the basis for efficient computation in $K[x]/(\mu_x)$
sections.mathContext: Power reduction is the computational content of the isomorphism $K[X]/(\mu_x) \cong K[x]$: to compute $x^k$ as a $K$-linear combination of $\{1, x, \ldots, x^{d-1}\}$ where $d = \deg(\mu_x)$.

sections.title: Section VI: Special Elements
sections.summary: Minimal polynomial divisibility for special algebraic elements: idempotent ($x^2 = x \implies \mu_x | X^2 - X$), involutory ($x^2 = 1 \implies \mu_x | X^2 - 1$), nilpotent ($x^d = 0 \implies \mu_x | X^d$)
sections.mathContext: Each condition $p(x) = 0$ gives $\mu_x | p$. For idempotents: $\mu_x | X(X-1)$, so $\mu_x \in \{X, X-1, X(X-1)\}$. For nilpotents: $\mu_x | X^d$, so $\mu_x = X^k$ for some $k \le d$.

sections.title: Section VII: Algebra Tower Reduction
sections.summary: For towers $K \subseteq L \subseteq A$: integrality lifts, $\mu_L(x) | \text{map}(\mu_K(x))$, and $\deg(\mu_L(x)) \le \deg(\mu_K(x))$. Equality holds when the mapped polynomial stays irreducible
sections.mathContext: In the tower $K \subset L \subset A$, the minimal polynomial over $L$ divides the base change of the one over $K$: more polynomials are available over $L$, so the degree can only decrease. Equality $\mu_L = \text{map}(\mu_K)$ holds iff $\mu_K$ stays irreducible over $L$.

conclusion.summary: This file develops two complementary theories: (1) modular arithmetic of polynomial evaluation via the minimal polynomial, showing that evaluation depends only on the remainder mod minpoly, and (2) base change behavior in algebra towers, proving degree can only decrease. All 23 theorems are fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The modular reduction theory provides the algebraic foundation for efficient computation in quotient algebras K[x]/(minpoly). The tower results extend the K-algebra invariance theory to base-ring-changing transformations.
